summary: Yu Yan Pang specializes in Buddhist studies and other fields. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui specializes in Buddhist studies. Tsui completed master's study at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu, studied under Sheng Yen and Robert E. Buswell Jr., and pursued doctoral study under Natasha Heller (attested 2018).

Yu-kwan Ng (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1968–1974) under Zongsan Mou and earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1990). Ng held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~1998–2011).
Yu-min Lee specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington and served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 1998).

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. Guo worked as a researcher at the Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute and held a post at the Jinling Sutra Publishing House.

Yudru Tsomu specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Tsomu earned a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark C. Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, having also studied with James E. Bosson and Wesley M. Jacobsen.
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.

Yuguang Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974). Katsuzaki later served as president (学長) of Taisho University (~2012–2015).

Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna. Kajiyama held professorial posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. Ito held posts at Bukkyo University (~1968–1997), Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen (~2000–2011), Shōjōke-in Temple (~2002–2007), and Chion-in Temple (~2011–2022).
Yujun Endo (1939–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Endo served as an associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University.
Yuka Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (attested 2015).

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Tohoku University and Kyushu University. Matsunaga held posts at Shuchiin University and Koyasan University, serving Koyasan as director (~1961–1995), professor, president, and professor emeritus.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and under Michael Hahn (attested 1987), later serving as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926) under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji. Sakamoto held a post at Toyo University and served as president of Rissho University (~1968–1972).
